documents.generated_document: CHIEF COMPLAINT: Follow-up diabetes and hypertension. HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient is a 62-year-old male, well known to the clinic, presenting for routine follow-up of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Essential Hypertension. He reports that his fasting blood sugars at home have been running high, typically in the 180-220 range over the last month. He admits he stopped taking his Metformin about three weeks ago because it was causing significant diarrhea and abdominal cramping. He denies polyuria or polydipsia. He does report a new onset of a pins-and-needles sensation in both feet, worse at night, which is interfering with his sleep. His blood pressure has been well controlled at home. He denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or visual changes. PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: T2DM, Hypertension, Hyperlipidemia. MEDICATIONS: Lisinopril 20 mg daily, Atorvastatin 40 mg daily, Metformin 1000 mg BID (currently holding). ALLERGIES: NKDA. REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or unexpected weight loss. Eyes: Negative for vision changes. CV: Negative for chest pain. Resp: Negative for shortness of breath. GI: Positive for diarrhea (when taking Metformin). Neuro: Positive for bilateral foot tingling. PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Vitals: BP 134/82, HR 78, Temp 98.6 F, RR 16, SpO2 98% on RA, BMI 31.2. General: Well-developed, well-nourished male in no acute distress. HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic. EOMI. Neck: Supple, no JVD. Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended, normal bowel sounds. Extremities: No edema. Neurologic: Decreased sensation to 10g monofilament testing on the plantar surface of bilateral feet. Reflexes are 2+ and symmetric at the patella and Achilles. LAB FINDINGS: Point of care A1c today is 8.9%, increased from 7.4% six months ago. Recent BMP and lipid panel from last week were reviewed; creatinine is stable at 0.9, LDL is 72. ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 1. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with hyperglycemia and new-onset peripheral neuropathy. The patient's diabetes is currently uncontrolled, largely due to medication non-adherence secondary to GI side effects from Metformin. We will discontinue the Metformin today. I will start him on Glipizide 5 mg daily before breakfast. For the painful diabetic neuropathy, we will initiate Gabapentin 100 mg TID. I have ordered a spot urine microalbumin/creatinine ratio today. A referral to Podiatry for comprehensive diabetic foot care has been placed. 2. Essential Hypertension. Clinically stable. Continue Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Hyperlipidemia. Stable on high-intensity statin. Continue Atorvastatin. Follow up in 4 weeks to check fasting blood sugars and assess tolerance to the new medication regimen.
documents.Justification: The CPT code 99214 is supported by an established patient office visit with a Moderate level of Medical Decision Making (MDM). The Number and Complexity of Problems Addressed is Moderate, as the patient presents with one chronic illness with exacerbation/progression (uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes with new-onset neuropathy) and two stable chronic illnesses (Hypertension and Hyperlipidemia). The Amount and/or Complexity of Data to be Reviewed and Analyzed is Moderate, meeting Category 1 requirements by reviewing three unique tests (POC A1c, BMP, Lipid panel) and ordering a new test (urine microalbumin). The Risk of Complications and/or Morbidity or Mortality is Moderate due to prescription drug management, specifically discontinuing Metformin due to adverse effects and initiating both Glipizide and Gabapentin. Meeting two of the three elements of MDM at the moderate level qualifies the encounter for 99214.
